ky_void_seal_controlled_substance.publicName: Void and seal a first Kentucky drug possession conviction
ky_void_seal_controlled_substance.legalName: Motion to Void a First Controlled-Substance Possession Conviction and Seal the Records (KRS 218A.275)
officialFormDependencies: AOC-334, Order Voiding Conviction and Sealing Records, Rev. 1-22 (component ky_void_seal_controlled_substance-proposed-order-2, required, tendered with the motion)
openBuildBlockers: KRS 218A.275(12) bars this relief to anyone who previously had a possession charge dismissed after a KRS 218A.14151 deferred prosecution. The controlling review does not record the bar; it changes who receives a packet at all and must be encoded and confirmed before the route is built (eligibility_branch).
openReleaseBlockers: The static legal propositions the motion asserts about the effect of voiding and sealing under KRS 218A.275(9) and (10) are unratified.
openCounselClassifications: Whether KRS 218A.14151 deferred prosecution (AOC-331 application, AOC-333 sealing order) should be added to the Kentucky mechanism denominator.

ky_void_seal_marijuana_synthetic_salvia.publicName: Void and seal a first Kentucky marijuana or synthetic drug possession conviction
ky_void_seal_marijuana_synthetic_salvia.legalName: Motion to Void a First Marijuana, Synthetic Drug or Salvia Possession Conviction and Seal the Records (KRS 218A.276)
officialFormDependencies: AOC-334, Order Voiding Conviction and Sealing Records, Rev. 1-22 (component ky_void_seal_marijuana_synthetic_salvia-proposed-order-2, required, tendered with the motion — same form as the KRS 218A.275 track)
openReleaseBlockers: The static legal propositions the motion asserts about the effect of voiding and sealing under KRS 218A.276(9) and (10) are unratified.

notes: Both Kentucky controlled-pleading tracks are genuine custom pleadings for the motion itself — the registry records no official form for either motion — but both tender the SAME official proposed order, AOC-334 Rev. 1-22. That is one distinct mandatory official-form handoff covering two tracks. No order text is drafted on either track.

Verification is affirmatively absent on both tracks rather than unknown: the registry states 'none required. The motion is not verified.' verificationStatute.citation is null on both, and no verification block is rendered. This is a deliberate contrast with the ND config's handling of a genuinely missing verification statute, where the source was silent and the requirement was flagged as unconfirmed.

ky_void_seal_controlled_substance carries an open legal-design build blocker: the KRS 218A.275(12) deferred-prosecution bar is not recorded by the controlling review and changes who receives a packet at all. The container is drafted and the blocker is flagged; the screening question exists on the track but the gate is not ratified. ky_void_seal_marijuana_synthetic_salvia has no build blocker.
No fee figure is quoted to a participant on either track. The recorded rule is that there is no filing fee for this proceeding, and a clerk who demands one is a self-help stop condition.

Neither track's mechanism appears anywhere in the compiled KY profile. The profile's five pathways are KRS 431.078, KRS 431.073, KRS 431.076 and two juvenile routes; the strings '218A.275', '218A.276', '27A.099' and 'AOC-334' appear nowhere in it, and the Kentucky Nationwide source corpus behind it is six expungement-side AOC PDFs, one PDF reference file and two HTML reference files. Both tracks therefore rest on the pinned registry entries. Regenerating the KY profile against a corpus that includes Chapter 218A would repair all three Kentucky lane-C1 tracks at once.

profile:terminology.allowedStateTerms for Kentucky is ['expungement', 'vacatur/vacation', 'pardon']. Neither 'voiding' nor 'sealing' is on that list, yet both are the remedy on these tracks. Recorded as a terminology conflict for F-review.

RENDERER COMPATIBILITY: a rendered sample of the canonical fixtures was produced in this worktree against src/lib/record-clearing/renderers/custom-pleading-renderer.ts and exposed three adapter defects, each recorded in the affected config's rendererCompatibility block. (a) usesCounty:true is a Pennsylvania-specific branch that emits 'the Court of Common Pleas of {county} County, Pennsylvania' and 'The Pennsylvania State Police' into any track that sets it; every Kentucky config here therefore sets usesCounty:false and carries the county through the {county} token in courtName/venueDescriptor, as the ND config does. (b) Fields deliberately left null under the sourced-content-only rule are stringified into the output as the literal word 'null' — in the caption party role, the parties block and the verification clause; the adapter must omit the line, not stringify. (c) A verification section is emitted even where the source affirmatively states the filing is not verified. No source-faithful field was altered to work around any of these.

FIXTURE SHAPE: fixture partyData uses the renderer's own PleadingRenderInput field names (petitionerName, petitionerAddress, otherNamesUsed). The movant/applicant role label comes from presentation.movantRole in the config, not from the fixture key.
